subject: snail
reasoning:
I'm planning out a stylized, compact snail model with a skeleton—sizing the body around 5cm and shell around 3-4cm, oriented facing +Z, with a root foot joint and a body chain running from tail to head.

I'm adding tentacle chains (long eye stalks, shorter lower feelers) and a jointed jaw with upper and lower parts, then working out the shell geometry as a spiral sweep with a tilted axis, shrinking tube radius from outer to inner whorls to avoid self-intersection.

I'm positioning the shell's aperture at the body's attachment point, figuring out the center height so the spiral sits naturally against the body, and planning the shell as a child joint/bone of the body for skinning. Then I'm shifting to the body itself, planning to loft it along a smooth path with a varying radius, and sketching the foot as a flatter ellipse shape.

Now I'm defining the radius function and path points for the body — wider near the neck, tapering at the tail, with the foot flattened against the ground and the head rising at the front.

For texture, I'm adding a mottled pattern to the body and spiral banding across the shell by painting stripes based on position along the tube and angle around it, mimicking the natural whorl pattern of a shell.

Now I'm setting up the body's joint chain, placing a root joint near the midpoint of the body path, then splitting into front and back chains of a few joints each that extend outward from that root.

Working out the taper radius function along the path, keeping height proportional to width so the tail stays grounded near the floor while thickening toward the body.

Now I'm sketching the eyestalk chains sprouting from the head, defining base-to-tip point sequences for a catmull curve.

Adding a small dark pink lower lip rather than a distinct mouth line, then setting up the shell joint centered on the core body, considering a small bright protrusion at the apex. I'm settling on the color palette: sandy mottled body, lighter sole, orange shell with dark stripes, and black eyes, then defining the spiral's center and orientation vectors for the shell geometry.

Working out the shell spiral's tangent direction so it curves backward and upward as it winds over the body, with about 2.5 turns from a small apex radius.

Checking proportions - the shell's height versus the body length feels chunky compared to a real snail, but I decide to keep it stylized rather than rescale, adjusting the spiral radius and center slightly to keep the top within reason. I'm moving on to the sweep operation now.
